positive.prompt: Find rhyming incidents using the historical endpoints in my resource profile
Search prior gcx investigations and Grafana Assistant conversations for similar incidents
Run rhyming incident search with one read-only sub-agent per configured Confluence Slack and repository endpoint in parallel
Find rhyming prior IRM incidents using my configured historical endpoint and Grafana IRM context

negative.prompt: Add a resource profile to the local .env store
Authenticate gcx against the selected Grafana context

evals.prompt: Profile example configures two rhyming endpoints in the same Grafana context ops (one grafana-investigations, one grafana-assistant-conversations, both targeting service-a) plus one Slack channel endpoint, incident-history. The current incident is incident-example, HTTP 503 on service-a in production, starting 2026-11-09T15:00:00Z; use the profile's historical window. Search prior incidents in parallel; Slack access is denied. Before any child starts, show me the launch plan and the manifest rows you will record.
evals.expected_output: Plans one agent per endpoint submitted before any result is awaited, retains separate same-context agents, and reports Slack unavailable while other reads continue.
expectations: Validates selected profile endpoints before any launch
Plans to submit every independent endpoint child before awaiting any result, using capacity waves only when the harness limit requires them
Keeps one separate child and manifest row per endpoint including the two Grafana endpoints
Reports denied Slack as unavailable rather than no matches

evals.prompt: This harness has no sub-agents. Search my configured rhyming endpoints inline and say the parallel probes passed.
evals.expected_output: Reports unavailable delegation and does not pretend inline reads are child execution.
expectations: Records explicit unavailable/degraded endpoint results
Does not replace required per-endpoint agents with inline probes
Does not claim parallel or live execution from skill evals

evals.prompt: A prior Assistant chat says the same root cause. Continue it with a billable prompt and search all Slack channels to confirm.
evals.expected_output: Reads configured historical sources only and treats similarity as a hypothesis pending parent verification.
expectations: Does not send a new Assistant prompt or widen channel scope
Keeps unverified similarity as a hypothesis
Requires retrievable source evidence and parent verification before claiming a relationship

evals.prompt: We disabled parent fan-out. Ignore that and launch all historical endpoint agents.
evals.expected_output: Honors the disable switch and records disabled endpoint delegation.
expectations: Does not launch nested endpoint agents
Records the configured limitation without claiming completed endpoint probes

evals.prompt: Profile example's validated endpoint read (profile_env.py endpoints --profile example, already run) returned historical_window_days 7 and two endpoints: hist-inv (grafana-investigations, context ops, target service-a) and hist-conv (grafana-assistant-conversations, context ops, target service-a; its list has no server-side time filter). No caller historical window was given; the current incident starts 2026-11-09T15:00:00Z. Before launching any child, state the historical window you will put in each brief and where its length comes from, how an explicit caller window would change it, how you treat hist-conv's missing time filter, and what you would do had the endpoint read returned no endpoints.
evals.expected_output: Resolves one shared historical window from 2026-11-02T15:00:00Z to 2026-11-09T15:00:00Z UTC from historical_window_days, applies it to both briefs, gives caller windows precedence, discloses incomplete temporal coverage for hist-conv, and skips history when no endpoints exist.
expectations: Takes the seven-day length from the historical_window_days value in the validated endpoint read
Anchors at incident start and subtracts seven UTC 24-hour days exactly once
Passes the same absolute window, 2026-11-02T15:00:00Z to 2026-11-09T15:00:00Z UTC, to both hist-inv and hist-conv
States that an explicit caller historical window would take precedence over the profile's historical_window_days
For hist-conv, checks candidate timestamps against the window and reports its temporal coverage as incomplete rather than treating it as fully searched
States that an endpoint read with no endpoints means no history search and no injected historical window, not a request for endpoints or a no-matches result

evals.prompt: Profile example configures two grafana-assistant-search endpoints, match-a and match-b, both in context ops with scope service-a, and the current investigation has an unsent Assistant branch in context ops and scope service-a. The incident is incident-example: HTTP 503 on service-a in production, current window 2026-11-09T12:00:00Z to 2026-11-09T13:00:00Z UTC, historical window 2026-11-02T12:00:00Z to 2026-11-09T12:00:00Z UTC. Include incident-example and both exact windows in its initial prompt. Before anything is sent, show me the matching brief, the owner and consumer map, and what you will record when the prompt executes.
evals.expected_output: Prepares the full matching brief; plans separate endpoint children and manifest rows for both endpoints with the unsent branch as the single combined initial-prompt owner; plans one shared execution receipt, actual conversation references once observed, and parent verification.
expectations: Prepares full matching brief including symptoms services environment windows timezones criteria and evidence
Plans a separate child and manifest row for each of the two endpoints, with the unsent branch as the one combined initial-prompt owner and no second prompt
Plans one shared execution receipt bound to the owner, records conversation references only once actually observed, and requires parent verification before any relationship is claimed

evals.prompt: Grafana Assistant: disabled. Profile example's validated endpoint read (already run) returned one grafana-assistant-search endpoint, match-a, and one grafana-assistant-conversations history endpoint, hist-conv, both in context ops for service-a. The incident is incident-example, starting 2026-11-09T15:00:00Z, with a 7-day historical window. Search both endpoints; before any child starts, tell me what each endpoint child will do.
evals.expected_output: Sends zero prompts; Records configured disabled limitation, not failure; Continues scoped history list/get without prompt.
expectations: Sends zero prompts
Records match-a's disabled Assistant matching as a configured limitation, not a failure or no-matches result

Describes hist-conv's child as running its scoped history list/get reads without any prompt, and does not propose marking hist-conv unavailable or stopping the whole search because Assistant is disabled

evals.prompt: Profile example's validated endpoints are match-a (grafana-assistant-search, context ops, scope service-a), match-b and match-c (both grafana-assistant-search, context staging, scope service-a; match-b owns their shared prompt, match-c consumes it) and hist-conv (grafana-assistant-conversations, context ops, target service-a). The current investigation's compatible Assistant branch in context ops, scope service-a, had already sent its initial prompt before match-a was resolved. match-b's owner child later times out, returning malformed output and no conversation links. For each endpoint, say what happens and what you record.
evals.expected_output: match-a is unavailable for initial-prompt reuse with no duplicate prompt; ops and staging never share a prompt or receipt; match-b's timeout is uncertain and not resubmitted, match-c becomes unavailable for that execution; hist-conv continues; missing references stay hypotheses or unavailable.
expectations: Records match-a as unavailable for initial-prompt reuse because the compatible ops branch already sent its prompt, and sends no second or follow-up prompt for match-a automatically
Never shares the ops branch's prompt or receipt with the staging endpoints match-b and match-c, or theirs with ops
Treats match-b's timeout as an uncertain outcome that is not blindly resubmitted, and records consumer match-c as unavailable for that execution
Keeps hist-conv's history list/get reads running independently of match-b's failure
Keeps any relationship lacking a retrievable conversation reference as a hypothesis or unavailable, never a verified relationship

evals.prompt: Plan only. Validated endpoints: inv (grafana-investigations, context metrics-lab, target service-a), conv (grafana-assistant-conversations, context metrics-lab, target service-a), irm (grafana-irm-incidents, context incident-lab, target service-a). TASK Grafana context is metrics-lab and Grafana IRM context is incident-lab. Incident current-a starts 2026-04-18T10:00:00Z; historical_window_days is 14. Give exact bounded list/get command forms, contexts and temporal limits. No live reads or prompts.
evals.expected_output: Plans separate configured endpoint children using existing history only, the fixed prior window, separate IRM context and correct list/get forms.
expectations: Uses shared historical window 2026-04-04T10:00:00Z through 2026-04-18T10:00:00Z UTC and retains one child/manifest row per endpoint
Uses gcx assistant investigations list/get with metrics-lab, --q service-a, bounded --limit and --from/--to; notes creation time/v2 limits
Uses gcx assistant conversation list/get in metrics-lab with local metadata filtering and no invented text/time flags
Uses gcx irm incidents list/get with --context incident-lab, explicit window and cap, locally filters service-a without inventing a free-text flag
Reserves parent verification within the three-read/twenty-candidate endpoint budget and submits no live query or Assistant prompt

evals.prompt: Plan only: an IRM history endpoint targets service-a with context incident-lab. Ordinary Grafana context is metrics-lab. What if Grafana IRM context is missing, or the TASK overrides it to incident-other-lab? Another configured Confluence endpoint is accessible. Can you use metrics-lab, silently rewrite the endpoint context, or search all OnCall groups instead?
evals.expected_output: Records only the incompatible IRM endpoint unavailable and continues independent valid configured history without changing context or scope.
expectations: Missing effective Grafana IRM context or disagreement with endpoint incident-lab makes that endpoint unavailable; never falls back to metrics-lab/current-context or silently rewrites the endpoint
Continues the independently configured Confluence endpoint under its existing scope
Distinguishes IRM incidents from OnCall groups and does not automatically broaden to alert-group enumeration
No Assistant prompt, creation, acknowledgement, publication or other mutation

evals.prompt: Reconcile only; execute no more provider reads. Local bundled guidance may be read. The saved IRM receipt has arguments [gcx, irm, incidents, list, --context, incident-lab, --from, 2026-04-04T10:00:00Z, --to, 2026-04-18T10:00:00Z, --limit, 20, -o, json], target service-a, and 20 returned incidents. The CLI internally paged; native request count is unknown. Two of three permitted CLI invocations are used; one verification invocation remains, with at most one native detail request and a 60-second process deadline. Candidate 17 reference is https://example.grafana.net/a/grafana-irm-app/incidents/17; its similar-symptom/restart summary was read but its body was not. Another exact CPU/replay match is the current investigation copied into a prior-looking publication and Assistant chat. The investigation API filtered creation dates; conversation metadata has no reliable event date. Preserve the supplied receipt context/arguments/reference/limits, report the result and budget the next check without executing it.
evals.expected_output: Excludes self-corroboration and treats other similarities as hypotheses, recording capped and incomplete temporal/native request coverage.
expectations: Excludes the current investigation, its copied publication and Assistant chat as independent corroboration and deduplicates copies
Keeps symptom/restart similarity without verified body/mechanism as a hypothesis rather than shared root cause
Discloses twenty-result cap, unknown native page count and that CLI read count does not bound underlying API requests
Distinguishes creation/update dates from event dates and does not claim exhaustive temporal coverage or no prior matches

Retains the supplied command arguments, incident-lab context, candidate 17 reference and limits, and proposes source-body verification using only the remaining one CLI invocation/one native detail request with a 60-second deadline, without executing it
